targets.authors: Gluth S, Spektor MS, Rieskamp J
targets.title: Value-based attentional capture affects multi-alternative decision making
targets.evidence_quote: Many eye-tracking studies on value-based decisions reported an influence of attention on choice: Options that are looked at longer are more likely to be chosen 12 , 16 , 17 , 28 – 32 . We tested this effect using a random-effects logistic regression analysis that regressed whether an option was chosen or not onto the option’s relative gaze duration while controlling for the option’s relative value. Again, the last fixation per trial was excluded from this analysis. In line with the previous literature, we found strong evidence for an influence of gaze on choice ( t (36) = 7.81, p < .001, d = 1.28, 95% CI = [1.45, 2.47]).

reasoning: Primary distractor-choice replication failed in both new experiments. The explicit successful replication of gaze influence names eight original papers as its tested set; these are independently included. Krajbich and Rangel (2011) also provides original data for a secondary reanalysis; this record is classified by its new-sample replication experiments. The reanalysis examines new distractor and fixation relationships rather than attempting numerical reproduction of original reported results.
